items.claim: “earliest-diverging liverwort lineage, sister to all other liverworts”; “monophyletic bryophyte clade”; “Liverworts lost stomata completely”
items.section: Front matter: lineage, stomata; Affinity and controversies
items.evidence: Sources support basal placement within liverworts, bryophyte monophyly and secondary stomatal loss; these are clade-level conclusions.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text; [Harris 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960982220304188), abstract; [Harris 2022](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/divergent-evolutionary-trajectories-of-bryophytes-and-tracheophyt/), abstract.

items.claim: “glomeromycotean-like”; “Endogone-like Mucoromycotina in at least six Haplomitriopsida species”; “could be a derived trait”
items.section: Affinity and controversies: Which fungus; Ancestral or derived
items.evidence: Carafa describes morphological resemblance; Bidartondo identifies Mucoromycotina in six species; Field confirms the experimental partners while allowing a derived origin.
items.source: [Carafa 2003](https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1469-8137.2003.00849.x), abstract and indexed full-text passages; [Bidartondo 2011](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3130224/), indexed full text; [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text.

items.claim: “No Haplomitriopsida fossil is known from the Late Ordovician to Early Devonian window in the sources read”
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Hübers and Kerp's abstract supports the sparse pre-Permian record, but cannot establish this class-wide absence; full text was inaccessible.
items.source: [Hübers and Kerp 2012](https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/geology/article-abstract/40/8/755/131004/Oldest-known-mosses-discovered-in-Mississippian?redirectedFrom=fulltext), abstract only.

items.claim: “Gessella … from the Early Permian of Western Sealand”
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Poulsen's abstract places the Gessella-bearing macroflora in the Upper Permian, contradicting the Wikipedia-derived Early Permian age.
items.source: [Poulsen 1974](https://doi.org/10.34194/raekke2.v101.6892), abstract reproduced in the indexed [ResearchGate record](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352976396_The_Lower_Palaeozoic_sequence_in_the_Slagelse-1_well_Stratigraphical_lithological_and_geochemical_evaluation); original full text inaccessible.

items.claim: “Field et al. (2015) quote Heinrichs et al. (2007) for the early Devonian, over 400 Ma”
items.section: Front matter: range.notes
items.evidence: Field repeats precisely this estimate; Heinrichs's original dating analysis could not be independently checked.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Discussion; [Heinrichs 2007](https://www.jstor.org/stable/25065733), inaccessible article landing page.

items.claim: “max: 3.0”; “16-25(-30) mm”; “female shoots … 6-7.5 mm wide”; “no minimum is given”
items.section: Front matter: height_cm, axis_diameter_mm; Model transfer: dimensions
items.evidence: Flora gives these shoot-height maxima and female leafy-shoot widths, without a minimum height or explicit bare-stem diameter.
items.source: [Flora of New Zealand, H. gibbsiae](https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/af2f0e33-1e92-480e-83a8-5a5bca62f57b), full species account.

items.claim: “Leafy stems unbranched above”; “rhizome … irregularly branched”; “three ranks”; “2-4-stratose basal field”
items.section: Front matter: branching, leaves
items.evidence: Flora describes unbranched aerial stems, a branching rhizome, three leaf ranks and a basal field two to four cells thick.
items.source: [Flora of New Zealand, H. gibbsiae](https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/af2f0e33-1e92-480e-83a8-5a5bca62f57b), full species account.

items.claim: “terminal”; “0.5 x 3-4 mm”; “rarely 2-4 sporophytes”; “seta … 20-25 mm”
items.section: Front matter: sporangium_position, height_cm; Model transfer: dimensions
items.evidence: Flora places sporophytes at the gametophore apex, usually singly, exceptionally two to four, and gives the stated capsule and seta dimensions.
items.source: [Flora of New Zealand, H. gibbsiae](https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/af2f0e33-1e92-480e-83a8-5a5bca62f57b), full species account.

items.claim: “23-29 micrometres”; “tetrads or diads”; “elaters 280-520 micrometres”; “One spore size range is reported”
items.section: Front matter: spores, heterospory; Model transfer: dimensions
items.evidence: Flora reports these dimensions and temporary spore cohesion. A single reported size range supports, but does not itself demonstrate, the homospory coding.
items.source: [Flora of New Zealand, H. gibbsiae](https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/af2f0e33-1e92-480e-83a8-5a5bca62f57b), full species account.

items.claim: “dioecious”; “antheridia 25-45 or more”; “about 20 archegonia”
items.section: Front matter: gametophyte
items.evidence: Flora gives separate sexes, at least approximately 25–45 antheridia per androecium and approximately 20 archegonia per gynoecium.
items.source: [Flora of New Zealand, H. gibbsiae](https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/af2f0e33-1e92-480e-83a8-5a5bca62f57b), full species account.

items.claim: “conducting_tissue: … non-lignified”; “Perforate water-conducting cells”; “cylinder of food-conducting cells”
items.section: Front matter: conducting_tissue
items.evidence: Conducting anatomy is supported, but the review treats bryophyte lignin as contested and supplies no species-specific assay establishing the categorical non-lignified state.
items.source: [Ligrone 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3310499/), indexed full-text vascular-tissue sections; [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text.

items.claim: “Over half the total biomass … is subterranean”; “no rhizoids at all”
items.section: Front matter: height_cm, rooting
items.evidence: Field explicitly reports both features for H. gibbsiae.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Discussion.

items.claim: “soil nutrients reach it only through Mucoromycotina fungi”
items.section: Model transfer: Chosen to contrast
items.evidence: Field infers high dependence; it does not establish exclusive fungal acquisition of every soil nutrient.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Discussion.

items.claim: “South Island NZ, April 2012”; “12 weeks, 50 micromol per m2 per s, 15/12 °C”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: Stock and chamber settings match; twelve weeks was acclimation, followed by twenty-one days of nutrient tracing before carbon labelling.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Methods.

items.claim: “reciprocal carbon-for-nutrient exchange”; “33P and 15N (ammonium) under both 440 and 1500 ppm”; “not significantly CO2-dependent”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: Results support reciprocal exchange, unchanged proportional carbon allocation and nonsignificant CO2 effects on nutrient-for-carbon efficiencies.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Results and Figures 3–5.

items.claim: “South Island, December 2013”; “gemma-propagated M. paleacea from Mexico”; “5 pots per treatment”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, second bullet
items.evidence: Methods confirm these origins and propagation; figure legends specify five replicates per treatment combination.
items.source: [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, Methods and figure legends.

items.claim: “over 2.4-fold at 440 ppm to over 90-fold at 1500 ppm, pooled with N. mirabilis”; “about twice as much 33P”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, second bullet; Cannot transfer, pooled-statements bullet
items.evidence: Ratios and phosphorus comparison match Results; 'pooled' is misleading: two partnerships are discussed jointly without defining a combined mean.
items.source: [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, Results and Figures 3–4.

items.claim: “fungal carbon under 2% of fixed carbon in all plants”
items.section: Model transfer: Can transfer, second bullet
items.evidence: The percentage concerns carbon reaching external mycelium inside mesh cores, not total allocation to all fungal tissues.
items.source: [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, carbon-allocation Results and Figure 5.

items.claim: “H. gibbsiae axenic and re-inoculated: the underground axes form only with the fungus”
items.section: Front matter: rooting; Model transfer: Can transfer, third bullet
items.evidence: Axenic plants lacked these axes; inoculation restored them within three months. Support is specific to the reported culture conditions.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, in-vitro Results and Figure 8.

items.claim: “Do not use … fluxes as field or Palaeozoic rates”; “CO2 at two levels only”; “1500 ppm taken from geochemical … models”
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, first bullet
items.evidence: Both use controlled microcosms and two CO2 treatments; the simulated palaeo-atmosphere derives from models. Transfer restrictions are justified audit inferences.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text; [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, Introduction and Methods.

items.claim: “Do not attribute … differences to the fungus alone”; “confounded in a three-species design”; “against data from an earlier experiment”
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, second bullet
items.evidence: Methods assign one host species per partnership; Field 2015 overlays earlier data. The confounding diagnosis follows from these designs.
items.source: [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, Methods; [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, experimental comparison.

items.claim: “Do not treat ammonium (2015) and algal necromass (2019) as interchangeable nitrogen sources”
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, fourth bullet
items.evidence: Methods distinguish labelled ammonium chloride from labelled Chlorella necromass.
items.source: [Field 2015](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024), full text, Methods; [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text, Methods.

items.claim: “Do not transfer the efficiency values to M. polymorpha”; “non-mycorrhizal”; “M. paleacea is a different species”
items.section: Model transfer: Chosen to contrast; Cannot transfer, fifth bullet
items.evidence: Bowman distinguishes non-mycorrhizal M. polymorpha from mycorrhizal M. paleacea; Field's experimental Marchantia is paleacea.
items.source: [Bowman 2022](https://academic.oup.com/plcell/article/34/10/3512/6670628), full-text review, Mycorrhizal interactions; [Field 2019](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819), full text.

items.claim: “Mucoromycotina-like endophytes occur in Pragian Rhynie plants”; “exchange in the fossils is inferred, never observed”
items.section: Front matter: range.notes; Model transfer: Cannot transfer, sixth bullet
items.evidence: Fossil anatomy supports fungal affinity, not measured exchange. Rhynie biostratigraphy permits Pragian to possibly earliest Emsian, rather than an exclusively Pragian assignment.
items.source: [Strullu-Derrien 2014](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.12805), full text; [Parry 2013 geological reply](https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/504426/1/Parry%20et%20al.%20%282013%20JGSL%29_NORA%20VERSION.pdf), full text.

items.claim: “Do not treat the Haplomitriopsida condition as ancestral for embryophytes, or its conducting cells as hydroids or xylem”
items.section: Model transfer: Cannot transfer, seventh bullet; Affinity and controversies
items.evidence: Ligrone distinguishes perforate conductors from hydroids and xylem; Harris reconstructs substantial reductive evolution, making direct ancestral extrapolation unjustified.
items.source: [Ligrone 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3310499/), indexed full-text vascular-tissue sections; [Harris 2022](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/en/publications/divergent-evolutionary-trajectories-of-bryophytes-and-tracheophyt/), abstract.

omissions: Axenic gametophytes were maintained for over two years. Fungal induction of underground axes therefore does not demonstrate obligatory fungal dependence for survival under all conditions. [Field 2015, full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.13024).

Fungal biomass was not quantified. Differences in nutrient delivery cannot be converted into intrinsic efficiencies per unit fungal biomass. [Field 2019, full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819).

Necromass nitrogen transfer does not establish direct fungal decomposition: microbial mineralisation, competition and community effects remain alternative mechanisms. [Field 2019, full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819).
The carbon measurement covers core mycelium; a model needs a separate allowance for fungal carbon outside that measured compartment. [Field 2019, full text](https://doi.org/10.1111/nph.15819).

Non-mycorrhizal M. polymorpha hosts other fungal endophytes, including growth-promoting isolates. Calling the contrast 'symbiont-free' elsewhere in the card is inaccurate. [Bowman 2022, full text](https://academic.oup.com/plcell/article/34/10/3512/6670628).

A primary report documents H. gibbsiae in Guangxi, China, so the stated geographic distribution is incomplete; disputed broader species circumscriptions warrant explicit treatment. [Han 2025, indexed full-text sections](https://www.sciencedirect.com/org/science/article/pii/S1314283625001228).
model_transfer_assessment: Fungal nutrition is an appropriate contrast, but M. polymorpha provides a conceptual comparison rather than an experimentally matched control. The 2015 exchange and culture observations concern H. gibbsiae; the 2019 numerical summary jointly describes two host partnerships and should not become a species-specific coefficient without extracting the separate results. Flora dimensions describe the species generally, not the isotope specimens. The existing limits correctly identify host–fungus confounding, nitrogen-source differences and uncertain fossil extrapolation. Add limits concerning unmeasured fungal biomass, microbial nitrogen processing, core-only carbon accounting, and the distinction between nonsignificance and demonstrated CO2 invariance.
overall: The card reproduces most morphological measurements and experimental findings accurately, but overstates exclusive fungal nutrition and total fungal carbon cost. Correct the Gessella age, qualify the conducting-tissue coding and experimental duration, and retain this exemplar for constrained mechanistic comparisons rather than quantitative Palaeozoic calibration.
